title: Ausbildung Germany 2026: Requirements, Pay and Visa
metaDescription: Ausbildung Germany 2026: B1 German, a school certificate and a training contract. Minimum pay €724 a month, 325+ occupations and a §16a visa route.
headline: Ausbildung in Germany 2026: Requirements, Pay, Visa and How to Apply

sections.title: What is Ausbildung?
sections.content:
Ausbildung is Germany's dual vocational training system. You sign a training contract with a company, work there most of the week, and spend the rest of the week at a vocational school, the Berufsschule, learning the theory. The Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training lists more than 325 officially recognised occupations, from nursing and mechatronics to IT, banking and hospitality.

Training usually lasts two to three and a half years and ends with a final chamber exam and a state-recognised qualification that is accepted across Germany and the EU. You are paid from day one, and the system is built to turn trainees into skilled workers: the Federal Employment Agency reported more than 270,000 unfilled training places in 2024.

sections.title: Who can apply: age, education and German
sections.content:
There is no legal upper age limit for Ausbildung when you hold a signed training contract, and the training visa under section 16a sets no age cap. Most successful applicants are between 18 and 35, and the separate visa for searching for a training place is only available to people under 35. Employers generally expect a completed school-leaving certificate, roughly 12 years of schooling, but a university degree is not required.

German is essential, because training and the classroom are conducted in German. The standard requirement is B1, proven with a certificate from Goethe-Institut, telc or ÖSD, while healthcare and nursing applicants almost always need B2. Many employers in other trades also prefer B2, so stronger German means a wider choice of places.

sections.title: What you earn in 2026
sections.content:
For training starting in 2026, the legal minimum training allowance is €724 gross per month in the first year, rising to about €854 in year two and €977 in year three. Most trainees earn more than the floor: collectively agreed rates averaged about €1,209 a month across all training years in 2025, and rates are renegotiated upward each year.

Nursing trainees earn roughly €1,340 to €1,490 in the first year, IT trainees around €1,000 to €1,200, and banking and finance trainees €1,100 to €1,300. After qualifying, skilled workers in these fields often start at €2,700 to €3,500 a month, so the training years are a genuine investment in a much higher salary.

sections.title: Visa, blocked account and how to apply
sections.content:
Non-EU citizens need a national visa for vocational training under section 16a of the Residence Act, applied for at the German embassy with a signed training contract and a B1 certificate. Your livelihood counts as secured when your training allowance is at least €1,048 gross or €822 net per month in 2026; if it is lower, you must show funds, usually a blocked account of €11,904 for the year.

If you have no contract yet, a separate search visa under section 17 lets you look for a training place in Germany for up to nine months, provided you are under 35 and can show about €1,091 a month. Find places through the Federal Employment Agency portal and the official Make it in Germany site, and after qualifying you can move onto a work visa and a settlement path.

faqs.q: Is there an age limit for Ausbildung in Germany?
faqs.a: No, there is no legal upper age limit for Ausbildung with a signed training contract, and the training visa under section 16a sets no age cap. Most successful applicants are between 18 and 35. The separate visa for searching for a training place is only available to people under 35, and older applicants may face extra questions at the interview.

faqs.q: What German level do I need for Ausbildung?
faqs.a: You need German at B1 level as the standard requirement for the training visa, proven with a certificate from Goethe-Institut, telc or ÖSD. Healthcare and nursing applicants almost always need B2, because patient contact demands stronger German, and many employers also prefer B2. Reaching B1 from zero usually takes 6 to 12 months of steady study.

faqs.q: How much does an Ausbildung trainee earn in 2026?
faqs.a: For training starting in 2026, the legal minimum training allowance is €724 per month in the first year, rising to about €854 in year two and €977 in year three. Most trainees earn more, with collectively agreed rates averaging about €1,209 a month. Nursing trainees earn €1,340 to €1,490, and qualified workers often start at €2,700 to €3,500 a month.

faqs.q: Do I need a blocked account for an Ausbildung visa?
faqs.a: Not always. With a signed training contract, your livelihood counts as secured when your allowance is at least €1,048 gross or €822 net per month in 2026. If your allowance is lower, or you apply for the search visa without a contract, you must show funds, usually a blocked account of €11,904. Check the exact figure with your German embassy.
